# Changelog

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-changelog.sh — do not edit by hand. -->

All notable changes to Nexspence, newest first. The release notes are written
when the release is cut; this file collects them.

The full release notes — including the Docker image matrix and the
essentials bundle — are on the [releases page](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/releases).

## v2.13.5

2026-11-25 — v2.13.5

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
* 89ddbcae2c445c9f63ab6c7e6ddb7fc922daef8b fix(api): serve the product version from a public endpoint (#825)
* e080c3cbd1b2cce6825eb44800ee038251e39207 fix(ci): cut the announced range from the tag's own history (#781)
* f3b68ebf27c9ed7becd48b45046f046161abd133 fix(pypi): serve relative links, so a proxy works without a configured base URL (#824)
### 📚 Documentation
* bc8d8985e4fc3affc30ae93f81b8387032cc586c docs: add the Alpine, RubyGems and R/CRAN guides (#820)
* e61242f81e79f96b8cc695827884a7ce002bbe04 docs: add the Conan, Conda and Terraform guides, and fix the group authentication and the Conan group search (#819)
* c31ef8243f850e0afa6362ac4abda054d5f19abb docs: add the Helm, Go modules and Cargo guides, and fix cargo search (#811)
* ad751d0ae48d0c31aa47e96a33cfb06785f74ef8 docs: add the NuGet, Raw and APT guides, and fix the partial repository update (#812)
* 0a27695f322e28ee6d36c3fb5fe9cbd58e25b66a docs: correct the format guides against the running server (#810)
* d3839e40c5c24e09d203cf94e90bd8e117d3aae3 docs: format guides, changelog generator, and script defaults on the real port (#803)
* 7db18342bf607c58f1195dcf60d7713f3d22fb01 docs: make the project discoverable — positioning, issue forms, sponsor tiers (#802)

### 🐳 Docker

| | |
|---|---|
| **Image** | `ghcr.io/nexspence/nexspence:v2.13.5` |
| **Platforms** | linux/amd64, linux/arm64 |

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nexspence/nexspence:v2.13.5
```

#### Quick start

Download **`nexspence-run-essentials-2.13.5.zip`** below (config +
image-pinned compose + Helm chart + monitoring + Keycloak realm + seed scripts),
extract it, rename `config.yaml.example` → `config.yaml`, and set the admin
password and JWT secret. (The full source is the **Source code** archive / `git clone`.)

| Mode | Command |
|------|---------|
| Single-node | `docker compose up -d` |
| Single-node + Monitoring | `docker compose --profile monitoring up -d` |
| Single-node + Keycloak SSO | `OIDC_ENABLED=true docker compose --profile keycloak up -d` |
| HA (2 nodes + nginx) | `docker compose -f docker-compose.ha.yml up -d` |
| HA + Keycloak SSO | `OIDC_ENABLED=true docker compose -f docker-compose.ha.yml --profile keycloak up -d` |

**Web UI:** single-node → `http://localhost:8081` · HA → `http://localhost:8080`

Native install (deb/rpm/macOS/Windows): see the
[documentation](https://nexspence.com/docs/).

## v2.12.0

2026-10-28 — v2.12.0

### ✨ Features
* 3921933333a13875bebece7f628c1c896c9fed07 feat(docker): refuse a manifest pull at or above a scan severity (#641) (#672)
* e5baf92f4089e98c3dbcd49faeff1452c3f0e12d feat(go): enforce minimum package age on Go proxies (#643) (#670)
* 8191c1ea5d460d7d817d18e3b61c4629f5a995f6 feat(helm,conda): enforce minimum package age on Helm and Conda proxies (#643) (#674)
* 4d1d51e6a7a9551bbd696ca1fc4155f16159c7fe feat(npm): implement registry search with group merging and scoped visibility (#710)
* 280ba51e8104376bfa1dcccd3f6dcaea088aef95 feat(nuget): enforce minimum package age on NuGet proxies (#643) (#673)

## v2.9.2

2026-10-03 — v2.9.2

## Security

This release fixes five vulnerabilities reported privately by @jorgemillan — thank you. **Upgrading is recommended for every installation.**

| Severity | Advisory | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | [GHSA-pg67-wh39-mx9j](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-pg67-wh39-mx9j) | apt repository signing key and passphrase returned by the repository read API |
| High | [GHSA-86xg-jx85-4hj7](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-86xg-jx85-4hj7) | LDAP login with a differently-cased username authenticates as the local or SSO account of the same name |
| High | [GHSA-jcgv-hchv-g397](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-jcgv-hchv-g397) | `..` path segment bypasses path-scoped content selectors |
| High | [GHSA-389h-4qc3-698w](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-389h-4qc3-698w) | A scoped API token can create an unscoped one |
| Medium | [GHSA-vpvp-9379-86x6](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-vpvp-9379-86x6) | Content-selector evaluator ignores negation |

> ⚠️ **If you run a signed apt repository**, treat its signing key as compromised: generate a new key, re-sign the repository, distribute the new public key and revoke the old one. Upgrading stops further exposure but does not un-expose a key already served.

Also review content selectors for `!=`, `!` or other operators: they now grant nothing, where they previously granted what they meant to exclude.

## v2.0.0

2026-08-19 — v2.0.0

> **Breaking.** The nexspence image no longer contains Trivy. After this upgrade, scanning of **Docker and OCI images** stops until you supply a Trivy binary. Everything else upgrades unchanged. Package scanning (Maven, npm, PyPI, Cargo) is unaffected — it uses OSV.dev and never needed Trivy. Scan results already in the database stay visible.

## Why

Trivy is ~150 MB of third-party software that rode inside every nexspence image whether or not anyone scanned, pinned to a version nobody chose and unchangeable without a nexspence release. Supplying it yourself means you pick the version and update it on your own schedule.

## What to do

**Kubernetes / Helm** — one value. The chart adds a `trivy-copy` initContainer that copies the binary out of the `aquasec/trivy` image into a shared `emptyDir` and points nexspence at it:

```yaml
scanning:
  enabled: true
  trivy:
    image:
      repository: aquasec/trivy
      tag: "0.70.0"
```

**Docker Compose** — the shipped file is already wired; a one-shot `trivy-init` service in the `scanning` profile fills a named volume that nexspence mounts read-only:

```bash
echo "NEXSPENCE_SCAN_TRIVY_ENABLED=true" >> .env
docker compose --profile scanning up -d
```

**Native install** — any normally installed Trivy works. `scan.trivy.bin` defaults to `trivy` resolved through `PATH`, so a package-manager install is found on its own:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y trivy      # or dnf install trivy, brew install trivy
```
```yaml
scan:
  trivy:
    enabled: true
```

Then restart nexspence — configuration is read at startup only.

## What nexspence tells you now

The scanner is probed with `<bin> --version`, which answers three questions at once: is the file there, will it run here, and which version is it. The answer is one of four states rather than one boolean, because pointing an operator at the wrong one costs an evening:

| state | meaning |
|---|---|
| `disabled` | `scan.trivy.enabled` is `false` — nexspence has not looked for a binary |
| `missing` | enabled, but nothing at the configured location and no `trivy` on `PATH` |
| `broken` | a file is there and will not execute — wrong architecture, truncated download, no execute bit |
| `ready` | it runs and reported its version |

Visible in **Admin → Security → CVE Scan**, at `GET /api/v1/security/scanner`, and in one log record at startup. A scan requested while the scanner is unavailable is refused `503` with that same sentence instead of failing obscurely, and automatic scan-on-upload skips image components rather than filling the history with errors. Once enabled, the binary probe re-runs at most once a minute, so supplying or replacing the binary is picked up without a restart.

## New configuration

`scan.trivy.*` — `enabled` (default `false`), `bin` (default `trivy`), `db_repository`, `java_db_repository`, `skip_db_update`, `cache_dir`, each with the usual `NEXSPENCE_SCAN_TRIVY_*` environment override. Air-gapped deployments mirror **both** `trivy-db` and `trivy-java-db`: the Java database is fetched separately the first time an image containing Java artifacts is scanned, and an unmirrored one dials `ghcr.io` and fails.

Registry credentials moved out of the Trivy argv into its environment — anything in argv is readable through the process table.

## Rolling back

`v1.39.0` is the last image that bundles Trivy; pinning it restores the previous behavior. No data is lost either way.

Full documentation: [docs/scanning.md](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/blob/main/docs/scanning.md) and the new **Image Scanning** page in the [online docs](https://nexspence.com/docs/#sec-scanning).

## v1.39.0

2026-08-19 — v1.39.0

## Docker: anonymous pull and authenticated push stop being an either/or

The `/v2/` ping answered `200` whenever *any* docker repository allowed anonymous access, which made every docker-family client select the anonymous scheme for the whole session and silently drop its stored credentials — one public repository broke authenticated push registry-wide, while `docker login` still reported success (#260).

The registry now speaks the docker token protocol. The unauthenticated ping always challenges with `Bearer realm="<scheme>://<host>/v2/token"`; clients with credentials trade them at `/v2/token` for a user token (so `docker login` verifies the password at login time, not one push later), and clients without credentials receive an anonymous token that names no user — per-repository RBAC decides their reads exactly as before. containerd, BuildKit and oras, which discover auth from the resource `401` rather than the ping, get the same challenge on data routes.

## Docker: the registry surfaces behave like a registry

- `GET /v2/_catalog` is served at instance level: the union of `<repository>/<image>` names the caller may read, with `?n=`/`?last=` pagination and per-repository RBAC applied (an anonymous caller sees only `allow_anonymous` repositories). Previously the path fell into the repository dispatch as a phantom repository named `_catalog` and answered `403` even to an admin (#261).
- The imageless `/v2/<repo>/tags/list` answers `NAME_UNKNOWN` instead of `{"name":"","tags":[]}` (#261).
- Docker/OCI repository names are validated against the distribution reference grammar on create, plus the reserved `/v2/` route names — a repository named `docker test` used to be created without complaint and was then unusable, because `docker tag host/docker test/img` is not parseable (#262).

## Promotion

- **Promote re-validates that the rule actually applies to the component.** `Promote` takes a caller-supplied `(rule_id, component_id)` pair and only *offered* matching rules, so any caller with promotion permission could promote an arbitrary component using whichever rule had the laxest gates, bypassing a stricter rule's `require_scan_pass` / `require_manual_approval`. The component's repository and path filter are now enforced up front for the whole batch, and re-checked at copy time (#255).
- Promotion to or from a repository on the implicit default blob store no longer fails with a raw NOT NULL constraint error: the store resolves to the seeded row's real id (#256).

## Replication

- Rule (re)scheduling and manual runs no longer inherit the HTTP request context, which `net/http` cancels the moment the handler returns — a rule could be reported as scheduled while its cron entry never materialized, and a manual run aborted almost immediately with no visible error (#254).
- A manual run that overlaps an in-flight run of the same rule answers `409` instead of `202`.

## Browse and UI

- The component listing shows per-artifact size (summed across assets) and push date, and the columns stay aligned under browser zoom and long asset paths (#257, #258).
- The blob-store migration progress UI reads real values again: `domain.BlobStoreMigration` carries the camelCase JSON tags its API contract requires (#253).

---

Reported by [@jorgemillan](https://github.com/jorgemillan) (#253–#256) and [@strasvet](https://github.com/strasvet) (#257–#262); implemented by [@strasvet](https://github.com/strasvet). Thank you both.

## v1.36.2

2026-08-14 — v1.36.2

## Security fix

### Routing rules on group repositories could be sidestepped with a `..` segment

A routing rule is the only path-level policy a `group` repository has — RBAC grants access to a repository, not to the paths inside it. The rule was matched against the request path exactly as it arrived, while the member that finally served the artifact normalized the path first. The string that was checked was therefore not the string that was served, and any rule could be sidestepped by spelling the path another way.

Affected deployments are those relying on routing rules to keep internal coordinates from resolving through a public proxy member (a dependency-confusion guard), or to hide a path prefix inside a federated group. Present since routing rules landed in v1.13.0, through v1.36.1. All formats.

**A group now refuses a request path carrying a `..` segment outright** rather than normalizing it, so nothing legitimate changes meaning on the way through — an artifact path never contains one, while a name that merely contains dots (`we..ird.txt`) is still served.

See [GHSA-xq6f-xp6w-c555](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/security/advisories/GHSA-xq6f-xp6w-c555). Upgrade if you use routing rules; if you do not, there is no path policy to bypass.

## Hardening

* The same guard covers the sub-index paths a merger asks the group for — those are built from member documents, which for a proxy member is whatever the upstream serves.
* **apt** — the architectures and components a group covers are read out of its members' `Release` and spliced into those paths. They now have to look like names (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$`), and the index matrix is capped at 64 architectures × 32 components. Without the cap, a member declaring a large matrix turned one `Release` request into a fan-out proportional to what it claimed — measured at 50 000 sub-index fetches for 500 architectures × 50 components. Real distributions are far below the cap (Debian ships ~10 architectures and 3 components).

Both were found while reviewing the group index-merging work that shipped in v1.36.1.

## Changelog
* fix(group): refuse request paths that carry a traversal segment (#242)

## v1.36.1

2026-08-14 — v1.36.1

## Highlights

### Group repositories publish metadata that describes what they serve

An apt or yum `group` with more than one contributing member served the real union of its members' package indexes, but relayed a single member's `Release` / `repomd.xml` verbatim — documents that describe *that member's own* indexes. apt and dnf verify every index against them before trusting it, so such a group either failed to sync with a hash-sum mismatch or silently hid every package the chosen member did not have.

* **apt** (#221) — `Release`/`InRelease` are now built for the group: architectures and components unioned across members, every checksum taken over the merged `Packages`/`Packages.gz` the group itself serves. `InRelease` is signed only with the group's own key. (`Release.gpg` keeps the previous plain fan-out — see the issue for why.)
* **yum** (#222) — `repomd.xml` is rebuilt over the merged documents, and `filelists.xml`/`other.xml` are merged across members instead of exposing only the first one, so `dnf provides` and changelog queries see every member.

Both take their checksums through the group layer rather than from locally stored assets, so **proxy members**, whose indexes come from upstream, are covered the same way. Verified against a live instance with a real `apt-get update` (two members contributing different architectures) and `dnf makecache` + `repoquery`.

### Distributed locking actually excludes (HA)

* **distlock** (#223) — `Release` deleted the lock key unconditionally, so a run that outlived its own TTL deleted the lock a second node had legitimately taken, letting a third one in behind it. It is now a compare-and-delete against the acquisition token (Redlock Lua script).
* **cleanup** (#224) — the admin "run all now" path took the lock, but the cron schedule — how cleanup actually runs — did not, so every node ran every scheduled policy concurrently and double-decremented reported blob-store usage. Every path now runs under a per-policy lock.
* **blob store migration** (#225) — losing the lock race no longer leaves a `pending` row that wedges the repository as "already active" (nor a leaked cancel func), and `ResumeAll` now releases the lock a crashed process left behind instead of blocking a restart for up to two hours.

### Build

* CI builds and scans with Go 1.26.6, picking up six reachable standard-library advisories (#228).

Thanks to @jorgemillan for the detailed reports behind all five fixes.

## Changelog
* fix(apt): build a group's Release from the union of its members (#230)
* fix(blobmig): close the lock lifecycle gaps in Start and ResumeAll (#229)
* fix(cleanup): run every scheduled policy under the distributed lock (#227)
* fix(distlock): release the lock only while this holder still owns it (#226)
* fix(yum): build a group's repomd over the repodata it actually serves (#231)
* chore(ci): build and scan with Go 1.26.6 (#228)

## v1.29.0

2026-08-06 — v1.29.0

This release closes every finding of the 2026-08-03 security audit — three high, eight medium, six low.

## ⚠️ Behaviour changes

Read this before upgrading; several defaults changed on purpose.

| Change | What to do |
|---|---|
| **CORS no longer defaults to a wildcard.** An empty `http.cors_origins` used to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, which let any website read responses from an internal instance. Empty now sends no CORS header. | Nothing, if the bundled UI is served from the same origin. Otherwise list the origins, or write `cors_origins: ["*"]` to keep the old behaviour. |
| **`auth.rate_limit_enabled` now defaults to `true`** (50 rps / 100 burst per identity). | Nothing for ordinary clients. Raise the limits if you drive heavy parallel CI from one address. |
| **`auth.anonymous_enabled` is now enforced.** It was read in exactly one place — to print a warning — so setting it to `false` changed nothing. | Nothing: it still defaults to `true`. Setting it to `false` now genuinely refuses every unauthenticated read. |
| **`X-Forwarded-For` is ignored unless you say who to trust.** gin trusted every proxy, so the client chose the IP in your audit log and evaded the rate limiter by rotating the header. | Set `http.trusted_proxies` to your reverse proxy. Empty means the real peer address is used. |
| **A Content-Security-Policy is served with the UI.** | Nothing. `http.csp` overrides it; `"off"` omits it. Artifact paths (`/repository/`, `/v2/`) are exempt so documentation sites in raw repositories keep working. |
| **SAML assertions are bound to the request that asked for them.** SP-initiated login previously could not succeed at all (the request ID was never passed to the parser). | Nothing — SAML login now works, and IdP-initiated assertions are refused by design. |

## New configuration

- `http.trusted_proxies` — peers whose `X-Forwarded-For` is believed. Empty trusts nobody.
- `http.csp` — override or disable the Content-Security-Policy.
- `outbound.allowed_internal_cidrs` — internal ranges the SSRF guard may reach, for on-prem upstreams.

## Security fixes

**High**

- `auth.anonymous_enabled` was a control that did nothing; it now gates every anonymous path, including the Docker `/v2/` handshake, which answers `401` with a challenge instead of `200`.
- CORS wildcard by default (above).
- `SetTrustedProxies` was never called, making rate-limit buckets evadable and the audit log forgeable.

**Medium**

- No ceiling on password guessing: rate limiting is on by default, and a new per-account backoff refuses further attempts with `429` + `Retry-After` **before** the bcrypt runs. Five failures are free; the penalty then doubles from 1s to a 15-minute cap. Shared across HA nodes when Redis is enabled, and enforced everywhere credentials are accepted — moving the guessing from `/api/v1/login` to Basic auth on `/repository/…` or `/v2/…` buys no fresh allowance.
- Failed credentials on the paths that fall through to anonymous access left no trace at all; they are now logged.
- The shipped OIDC `cookie_key` is refused at startup while OIDC is enabled, like the JWT secret and admin password already were.
- SSRF: the guard existed and covered proxy, webhook and replication targets; it gained the ranges Go's `IsPrivate` misses (CGNAT, broadcast, multicast) and an opt-out for on-prem upstreams.
- SAML assertions are bound to their AuthnRequest (above).
- A CSP now blunts any future XSS against the token in `localStorage`.
- Health probes were registered before the middleware chain, so they ran without `Recovery` — a panic in the readiness path took the process down. `/readyz` also hit Postgres and Redis on every unauthenticated request; healthy results are memoized briefly.
- Frontend dependencies updated (undici, postcss, jsdom, globals, jest-dom).

**Low**

- Backup import spools blob payloads to disk instead of holding an entire archive in memory, and caps entry count as well as entry size.
- The website image runs as an unprivileged user.
- Presign and lifecycle handlers check for admin themselves, so mounting them later cannot expose every blob.
- Subdomain values are validated before being spliced into a URL path.
- `.gitleaks.toml` silences the ~215 documentation and fixture matches so a real leak would stand out.

## Known issue

Backup **export** does not include blob payloads — the archive carries metadata only, so a restore recreates assets without their content. Found while verifying this release; it predates it and is not fixed here.

## v1.22.0

2026-07-24 — v1.22.0

## Highlights

This release fixes six reported issues in proxy repositories, cleanup policies,
S3 storage, and the browse UI, and adds outbound-proxy support for upstream
fetches.

### ✨ Features
- **Outbound HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy for proxy repositories (#79)** — upstream fetches
  can now traverse a proxy, configured globally (`proxy.*` config / `HTTP(S)_PROXY`
  env) or per repository (`proxy_config.http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`socks5_proxy`/
  `no_proxy` + optional auth). An explicitly configured internal proxy is allowed
  while the SSRF guard still blocks direct internal upstreams.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- **Initial S3 config now works (#81)** — with `storage.default_type: s3`, the
  `default`/`docker` blob stores are reconciled to S3 on startup, so they appear
  in the Blob Stores list and repo-create dropdown and repositories write to S3.
- **APT/proxy metadata refreshes (#77)** — proxied repository metadata
  (`InRelease`/`Release`/`Packages`, npm packuments, yum/pypi indexes) is now
  revalidated on a TTL (`proxy_config.metadata_max_age`, default 10 min) via
  conditional requests; immutable artifacts still serve from cache. Fixes
  "Release file … is expired".
- **Proxy artifact delete (#75, #76)** — cached proxy files get real component
  coordinates, and the browse UI deletes by asset path, so npm proxy deletes no
  longer silently no-op and apt proxy deletes no longer 400.
- **Browse pagination (#80)** — the component list honours `?offset=`, so the
  Browse pager pages instead of re-showing page 1.
- **Cleanup policies (#62)** — clear-all policies run instead of being silently
  skipped; manual runs report their outcome; last-run stats persist; blobs are
  deleted from the asset's own store (S3/group); orphan components are pruned;
  dry runs no longer loop.
- Bumped `golang.org/x/text` to v0.39.0 (GO-2026-5970).

**Full details:** PR #82.

## v1.19.0

2026-06-25 — v1.19.0

## 🎉 Nexspence is now fully open source

### ✨ Features
- **Nexspence is now fully open source.** The complete source — Go backend, React/TypeScript frontend, format handlers, deploy assets (Helm, Compose, HA), seed scripts and the website — is now public under **AGPLv3** at `github.com/nexspence/nexspence`. Previously only run-essentials were mirrored; the entire development tree is now open to read, build, audit, self-host and contribute.
- Releases now build from this repository's own tree — the run-essentials mirror sync step was removed (#11).

## v1.14.0

2026-06-08 — v1.14.0

### ✨ Features

- **Native installers** — Linux `.deb`/`.rpm`, macOS & Windows archives built by GoReleaser, with systemd / launchd / Windows-service integration. The binary now embeds the web UI (self-contained, no separate frontend needed). New [docs/install-local.md](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/blob/main/docs/install-local.md) covers native setup plus reverse-proxy (nginx/Caddy) and multi-node load-balancer configs. Requires external PostgreSQL.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

_No bug fixes in this release._

### 💾 Native install (no Docker)

Download the package or archive for your platform below, then point it at an external PostgreSQL. Full guide: [docs/install-local.md](https://github.com/nexspence/nexspence/blob/main/docs/install-local.md).

| Platform | Asset |
|----------|-------|
| Debian / Ubuntu | `nexspence_1.14.0_linux_amd64.deb` · `nexspence_1.14.0_linux_arm64.deb` |
| RHEL / Fedora / SUSE | `nexspence_1.14.0_linux_amd64.rpm` · `nexspence_1.14.0_linux_arm64.rpm` |
| macOS | `nexspence_1.14.0_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` · `nexspence_1.14.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` |
| Windows | `nexspence_1.14.0_windows_amd64.zip` · `nexspence_1.14.0_windows_arm64.zip` |

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo dpkg -i nexspence_1.14.0_linux_amd64.deb
sudo nano /etc/nexspence/config.yaml   # set database.dsn, jwt_secret, admin_password
sudo systemctl enable --now nexspence  # → http://localhost:8081
```

Verify downloads against `checksums.txt`.

## v1.13.0

2026-06-08 — Nexspence v1.13.0

### ✨ Features

- **Terraform provider `nexspence/nexspence` v0.1.0.** Manage Nexspence as code: `nexspence_repository` (hosted/proxy/group, all 14 formats), `nexspence_blobstore` (local/S3), `nexspence_user`, `nexspence_role`, `nexspence_content_selector`, `nexspence_privilege`, plus `nexspence_repository`/`nexspence_repositories` data sources. Built on `terraform-plugin-framework`, authenticates via `nxs_*` token or basic auth, and is published on the Terraform Registry. Source: [nexspence/terraform-provider-nexspence](https://github.com/nexspence/terraform-provider-nexspence).
- **Ready-to-apply Terraform example (`deploy/terraform-example/`).** A complete set of manifests exercising every provider resource and data source against a local stack on `:8080` — 14 formats × hosted/proxy/group, local + S3/MinIO blob stores, and the full content-selector → privilege → role → user RBAC chain. Ships a step-by-step README (bring up the stack, enable S3, `init`/`apply`) and documents the S3-endpoint gotcha (the endpoint is dialed by the Nexspence **server**, so it must be an in-network address). The in-app Terraform docs page gained a Blob Stores (local & S3) example.
- **Terraform provider v0.2.0 — four new resources.** `nexspence_cleanup_policy` (scheduled cleanup: age/last-downloaded/retain-N, attach to repos via `cleanup_policy_ids`), `nexspence_routing_rule` (ALLOW/BLOCK path rules), `nexspence_webhook` (HMAC-signed outbound event webhooks), and `nexspence_promotion_rule` (build promotion with scan-pass and manual-approval gates). The example manifests, in-app docs, and website now cover all of them, and the website landing page advertises the provider with a live registry version.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

_No bug fixes in this release._

### 🔧 Maintenance

- Dependency bumps: `runc` 1.2.3 → 1.2.8, `github.com/docker/cli`, and dev-deps `vitest` / `@vitest/coverage-v8`.

## v1.12.2

2026-06-06 — Nexspence v1.12.2

### ✨ Features


### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Audit log: client IP no longer shows a `/32` suffix.** The `remote_ip` column is a Postgres `INET`, and reading it back via `remote_ip::text` returned CIDR form (e.g. `192.168.1.100/32`). The audit list/stream queries now read it via `host(remote_ip)`, so the bare client IP is returned.

### 🔧 Quality / Tooling

- **Lint debt cleared — three more linters now gate CI.** Enabled revive `unused-parameter` and `exported`, plus `nilnil`, in `.golangci.yml` and drove all findings to zero: renamed 13 unused parameters to `_`, documented 281 exported symbols with Go doc comments (mocks exempted), and converted the repository layer off the `(nil, nil)` "not found" convention.
- **Repository layer now reports not-found via a `repository.ErrNotFound` sentinel** instead of `(nil, nil)`. All 27 postgres lookup sites and the in-memory mocks return the sentinel; `service.ErrNotFound` aliases it so existing handler 404 mapping is unchanged; service/handler/format callers translate it where the old nil branch carried specific behavior (idempotent delete, proxy cache-miss, existence pre-checks, group-member validation). `nilnil` is now enabled to keep the convention from creeping back.

## v1.12.0

2026-06-04 — Nexspence v1.12.0

### ✨ Features


### 🐛 Bug Fixes

_No bug fixes in this release._

### 🔧 Quality / Tooling

- **Frontend test suite from scratch (Track C)** — stood up Vitest + React Testing Library + MSW v2 + jsdom and wrote **449 tests** taking the React frontend from 0% to **95.1% lines / 95.1% statements / 83.7% branches / 80.2% functions**. Covers `authStore` and the axios `client` (interceptors, 401 redirect, error extraction) at 100%, all 6 components (holo kit, Select/MultiSelect portal dropdowns, TagEditor, Wizard, Layout), and all 14 pages (Login + OIDC/SAML callbacks, Repositories, Users, Security 8-tab, Cleanup, Admin 9-tab, Browse raw+docker trees, Search, Audit, Migration, Monitoring, Docs) plus the App router/guards. Shared test infra: MSW request handlers per API endpoint, typed fixtures, and a `renderWithProviders` (MemoryRouter + QueryClient + auth seeding) helper. Production `tsconfig.json` now excludes test files (so `tsc && vite build` stays green) with a dedicated `tsconfig.test.json` (`npm run typecheck:test`) keeping tests type-checked. New CI `frontend` job runs the build, the test type-check, and `vitest --coverage` with an 80% threshold gate. Website counter 1280→1729.
- **Format handlers + global CI coverage gate (Track B Phase 5)** — brought all 17 `internal/formats/*` packages from 38–77% to **≥80%** (repoproxy 38%→85%, npm 54%→94%, conda 57%→88%, terraform 57%→87%, pypi 64%→86%, yum 62%→89%, maven 64%→85%, gomod 66%→88%, docker 66%→92%, and 8 more). Added a new CI `coverage` job that enforces a per-package ≥80% unit-test floor across all `internal/*` packages (excluding db/logger/config/storage/testutil which have integration or no-logic exclusions). Fixed BUG-33: `TestAuditMiddleware` test-only data race — replaced `time.Sleep` + direct slice reads with `awaitAudit()` polling via the new thread-safe `AuditRepo.Snapshot()` method; all tests now pass cleanly under `-race`. 1280 unit tests passing. Website counter 1005→1280.
- **Service layer test coverage (Track B Phase 4)** — added table-driven tests for every previously-uncovered or low-coverage service (58.9% → **80.4%**): new `rbac_service_test.go` (0%→93%; CanAccessRepo admin-bypass, CEL expression evaluation, FilterRepos/Paths/DockerRows/Components/Assets), `user_service_crud_test.go` (0%→88%; Create/List/Get/GetByID/Update/ChangePassword/SetPassword/Delete/GetUserRoles/SetUserRoles/ValidateToken), plus gap-filling extra test files for repository_service, promotion_service, cleanup_service, backup_service, replication_service, scan_service, and blob_store_migration_service. 1005 unit tests pass. Website counter 815→1005.
- **Storage layer test coverage (Track B Phase 3)** — added unit tests for `LocalBlobStore` (Put/Get/Delete/Exists/Size/ListKeys/UsedBytes via `t.TempDir()`), `Registry` (Get cache hit/miss/invalidate, NewFromConfig, unknown type), and `NewBlobStoreFromConfig` (local + s3 validation). Added `integration`-tagged S3 tests via dockertest MinIO covering the full S3BlobStore interface (Put/Get/Delete/Exists/Size/ListKeys/UsedBytes/PresignGetURL/PresignPutURL/ConfigureLifecycle). Combined unit+integration coverage: **85.9%**. CI `integration` job extended to run storage tests with a ≥80% floor.

## v1.11.0

2026-06-04 — Nexspence v1.11.0

### ✨ Features

- **Demo video in the README** — added an inline product demo (`docs/assets/demo.mp4`) at the top of the README so the project's UI and workflow are visible at a glance on the repo landing page.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Frontend lint restored** — added a flat `eslint.config.js` (ESLint 10 dropped `.eslintrc`/`--ext`), wired `typescript-eslint` + react-hooks + react-refresh, and fixed the `lint` script. `npm run lint` now passes clean (0 problems). Cleared all findings it surfaced: replaced ~15 `any` error/catch sites with a typed `apiErrorMessage(e, fallback)` helper + `ApiError` interface in `api/client.ts`, fixed empty catch blocks and a side-effect ternary in SearchPage, and wrapped render-derived arrays (`items`/`allItems`) in `useMemo` to satisfy `exhaustive-deps`. Enabled the full react-hooks v7 strict ruleset (React Compiler lints: purity, static-components, refs, set-state-in-render, …) — fixed the one real finding (`SidebarDetail` was declared inside render; now a `renderSidebarDetail()` helper) and turned off the two dataflow rules that misfire on idiomatic hand-written React (`set-state-in-effect`, `immutability`).
- **Backup archive truncation now surfaced** — `BackupService.Export`/`ExportRepo` used `defer gw.Close()`/`tw.Close()` and returned `nil` even if the final gzip trailer or tar end-of-archive blocks failed to flush, silently producing a truncated/corrupt archive. Both now use named-return error propagation so a Close error surfaces when the body otherwise succeeded. (Surfaced by the golangci-lint errcheck pass.)
- **Proxy cache-write error formatting** — `repoproxy` built its cache-write error with `fmt.Errorf("...copyErr=%w putErr=%w", copyErr, putErr)` where one error can be nil when the branch fires, rendering the malformed `%!w(<nil>)`. Now uses `errors.Join(copyErr, putErr)`, which drops nil errors and yields a clean wrappable error.
- **Blob-store migration context leak** — the `context.WithCancel` cancel func in `BlobStoreMigrationService` was never invoked on the migration goroutine's exit paths (a context resource leak). `cancel()` now runs in the goroutine's cleanup defer on every exit path.
- **Repository NULL-column scan bugs (found by the new integration tests)** — three real production bugs the postgres integration suite surfaced and fixed: (1) `AssetRepo.scanAsset` could not read NULL `sha1`/`sha256`/`md5` checksums (assets stored without a computed digest), now read via `sql.NullString`; (2) `ComponentRepo.UpdateExtra` silently no-oped when the existing `extra` jsonb was NULL, dropping the merged update; (3) `ReplicationRepo.scanRule` could not read a NULL `last_run_status`, so `GetRule`/`ListRules` failed for every never-run replication rule — now read via `sql.NullString`.

### 🔒 Security

- **Tighter blob directory permissions** — `LocalBlobStore` now creates blob directories with `0o750` (was `0o755`); these are app-owned and served through the app, so group/other write/traverse is unnecessary.

### 🔧 Quality / Tooling

- **golangci-lint v2.12.2 adopted** — added a tuned `.golangci.yml` (v2 schema) enabling the standard set plus error-handling (errorlint, bodyclose, sqlclosecheck, rowserrcheck, nilerr) and style/security linters (revive [curated rule subset], gocritic, gosec, misspell, unconvert, nakedret, gocyclo, whitespace, usestdlibvars), with `max-same-issues`/`max-issues-per-linter` uncapped so the gate never hides findings. Pinned via `make lint` (Go module proxy, `v2.12.2`) and enforced by a new CI `lint` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). All findings resolved to zero; security suppressions (md5/sha1 protocol checksums, content-addressed blob path) carry inline justifications.
- **Postgres repository layer test coverage (Track B Phase 1)** — added a dockertest-based integration harness (`internal/testutil/pgtest`, `integration` build tag) that boots an ephemeral Postgres, applies the real migrations, and runs comprehensive tests for all 21 repositories in `internal/repository/postgres`, taking the package from ~0% to **87%** line coverage. A new CI `integration` job enforces an 80% floor. Tests are independent (each truncates its own tables) and the default `go test ./...` stays Docker-free (tag-gated). Three real NULL-scan/merge bugs were found and fixed in the process (see Bug Fixes).
- **Deferred (future tracks):** revive's `exported` doc-comment rule (~446 sites), `unused-parameter`, `unexported-return`, and `var-naming` were intentionally left disabled (high-churn or behavior-changing); migrating the repository layer from `(nil, nil)`-means-not-found to an `ErrNotFound` sentinel, and fixing a pre-existing `TestAuditMiddleware` test-only data race (production code is correct — the test reads a mock's slice without synchronizing with the fire-and-forget audit goroutine), are tracked for the backend test-coverage track.

## v1.10.1

2026-05-29 — Nexspence v1.10.1

### ✨ Features

- **Website favicon + custom error pages** — added a browser-tab favicon (`/assets/favicon.png`, 64×64 from the logo) and apple-touch-icon, linked from both the main site and `/docs/`. Added styled `404` / `403` / `50x` error pages matching the dark glassmorphism theme; nginx now serves a real 404 for unknown paths (was silently falling back to the homepage).


### 🔒 Security

- **Dependency CVE sweep (Trivy + Grype verified)** — patched all vulnerabilities found in the container image's application layer. Upgraded `russellhaering/goxmldsig` v1.4.0 → v1.6.0 (CVE-2026-33487, HIGH — XML Digital Signature integrity bypass affecting SAML/SSO validation), `Azure/go-ntlmssp` v0.1.0 → v0.1.1 (CVE-2026-32952, MEDIUM — NTLM challenge DoS), and `jackc/pgx/v5` v5.9.1 → v5.9.2 (CVE-2026-41889, LOW — SQL injection under specific query conditions). Pinned the Go toolchain to **1.26.3** (go directive + `golang:1.26-alpine` build image) to pull in the patched standard library (closes a batch of HIGH/MEDIUM stdlib CVEs: net/http2 SETTINGS DoS, mail-parsing, ReverseProxy, LookupCNAME). A fresh `trivy rootfs` scan of the 1.26.3-built binary reports **0 vulnerabilities**.

### 🔧 Maintenance

- **Dependency refresh** — updated all remaining Go modules to latest within-major (AWS SDK v2, cel-go, prometheus/client_golang, redis/go-redis, zap, goose, golang.org/x/{crypto,net,sys,text}, …) and bumped frontend packages (react 19.2.6, vite 8.0.14, react-router-dom 7.16, @tanstack/react-query 5.100, lucide-react 1.17, axios 1.16, eslint 10.4, plus date-fns 4 / pretty-bytes 7). Build image bumped to Node 24 (Active LTS). 474 Go tests pass; frontend `tsc` + Vite build clean.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Docs changelog now auto-refreshes** — `/docs/` cached the GitHub Releases list in `sessionStorage` with no expiry, so an open session never picked up newly published releases. Added a 5-minute TTL (`{ts, releases}` envelope) and bumped the cache key to `nx_releases_v2` so existing stale caches are ignored immediately.

## v1.9.1

2026-05-26 — Nexspence v1.9.1

### ✨ Features

**Phase 68 complete (2026-05-25)** — Extended Monitoring

- **Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint** — Bearer-authenticated (JWT or `nxs_*` token); 8 custom metrics: `nexspence_requests_total`, `nexspence_request_duration_seconds`, `nexspence_artifacts_total`, `nexspence_bytes_stored_bytes`, `nexspence_downloads_total`, `nexspence_artifacts_deleted_total`, `nexspence_goroutines`, `nexspence_memory_alloc_bytes`
- **Docker Compose monitoring profile** — `docker compose --profile monitoring up` starts Prometheus v2.51.0 + Grafana 10.4.0; pre-built dashboard with 8 panels (req/s, error rate, latency p95, artifacts, storage, downloads, goroutines, memory); can also run standalone via `deploy/monitoring/docker-compose.yml` pointed at any Nexspence instance
- **Combine with other profiles**: `OIDC_ENABLED=true docker compose --profile keycloak --profile monitoring up`
- **History API** — `GET /api/v1/metrics/history` returns last 360 data points (1 hour at 10s intervals) from an in-memory ring buffer
- **Repo metrics API** — `GET /api/v1/metrics/repos` returns top 10 repositories by downloads and storage size
- **UI — MonitoringPage 3 tabs**: Overview (existing stat cards), Charts (req/s, error rate, storage growth line/area charts via recharts, auto-refresh 30s), Repositories (top-10 table with sort toggle)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **User creation now persists roles** — `UserService.Create` was silently ignoring the `roles` field; users created via the REST API or seed scripts now get their role assignments saved
- **System Admin blank screen fixed** — `recharts` was missing from `node_modules`; running `npm install` in `frontend/` after pulling is required; added React `ErrorBoundary` so future render errors show a recoverable fallback instead of wiping the entire page
- **Monitoring page crash ("t is not a function") fixed** — the production build crashed on `/admin?tab=monitoring`. Root cause: `es-toolkit`'s `./compat/*` package export has no `import` condition (CJS only), so recharts' `es-toolkit/compat/*` imports resolved to CommonJS, which Vite 8/rolldown's interop miscompiled into a self-shadowing `var require_X = require_X()` that threw at chunk init. Fixed with a `vite.config.ts` plugin that redirects `es-toolkit/compat/<name>` to its ESM `.mjs` build (default-export interop shim), so the subtree bundles as pure ESM
- **Docker Compose default config mount fixed** — `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.ha.yml` now default to `./config.yaml` instead of `./config.yaml.example`; the previous default caused a `read /app/config.yaml: is a directory` crash when `config.yaml.example` was extracted as an empty directory from the release zip
- **Docker bind-mount on Mac fixed** — `config.yaml.example` is now bundled in the image as `/app/config.yaml`; without a file at that path Docker Desktop (Mac) created a directory and failed with `not a directory` on bind-mount
- **README logo fixed** — logo path updated to `docs/assets/logo.png` which is synced to the public repo; the previous `frontend/src/assets/logo.png` path was broken on github.com/skensell201/nexspence
- **Role privileges not saved on create/update fixed** — `RoleHandler.Create` and `Update` accepted `privileges` in the JSON body but never wrote to `role_privileges`; `SetPrivileges` was never called, so the CS → Privilege → Role chain (e.g. from `seed-rbac.sh`) was always broken
- **Monitoring profile missing from HA Compose fixed** — `--profile monitoring` was silently ignored when using `docker-compose.ha.yml` because Prometheus/Grafana were only defined in the single-node `docker-compose.yml`; added both services to `docker-compose.ha.yml` with a dedicated `deploy/monitoring/prometheus-ha.yml` that scrapes both `nexspence_1:8081` and `nexspence_2:8081`

## v1.8.1

2026-05-15 — Nexspence v1.8.1

### ✨ Features

* **Staging & Build Promotion** — controlled artifact promotion workflow between repositories (e.g. `staging-maven → prod-maven`). Admins define promotion rules with optional CEL path filters, scan pass requirements, and manual approval gates. Users promote individual components from the Browse detail panel or bulk-select components via checkboxes. Auto-approved promotions execute immediately (blob copy + metadata re-registration in target repo); manual-approval requests queue in the Admin → Promotion tab for an admin to approve or reject with a note. Webhook events `promotion.requested`, `promotion.approved`, `promotion.rejected`, `promotion.done` are dispatched for each state transition. API: `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/promotion/rules`, `POST /api/v1/promotion/promote`, `GET /api/v1/promotion/requests`, `POST /api/v1/promotion/requests/:id/approve|reject`, `GET /api/v1/components/:id/promotion-rules`.
* **nexspence.online website** — full product site added to `website/` with interactive architecture diagram, install guide (Docker Compose variants, Helm with 5 networking options), feature comparison vs Nexus OSS, and brand icons for all 14 formats. Served via nginx Docker profile: `docker compose --profile website up -d`.
* **AGPLv3 License** — `LICENSE` file added to the repository.

### 📚 Documentation

* **README rewritten** — shortened from 618 → 245 lines with links to dedicated docs instead of inline content.
* **`docs/deployment.md`** — complete deployment reference: Docker Compose (standard, MinIO, HA, Keycloak SSO), From Source, and full configuration reference table.
* **`deploy/helm/nexspence/README.md`** — full Helm reference: all 5 networking variants (nginx, Traefik, Cilium ingress, Istio Gateway, Cilium Gateway API), external PostgreSQL, S3 storage, HPA, upgrade and uninstall instructions.

## v1.7.4

2026-05-13 — Nexspence v1.7.4

### 🎨 UI / UX

* **Sidebar footer redesign** — replaced the cluttered footer with a pill-shaped command bar: circular gradient avatar, username, two circular icon buttons (API Tokens / Sign Out). Collapse is now an explicit chevron button. In collapsed mode the bar becomes a single avatar circle.
* **Documentation moved to nav** — "Documentation" promoted to its own **DOCS** section in the sidebar nav with cyan accent styling.
* **Sidebar scroll fix** — footer always pinned at the bottom; only the nav list area scrolls internally.
* **Profile modal** — token creation form restructured to two rows (Token name / Expiry + Create); Create button replaced animated holographic gradient with calm blue.

### ✨ Features

* **Helm chart** — production-ready Helm chart under `deploy/helm/nexspence/` with pluggable ingress (nginx, Traefik, Cilium ingress-controller) and API Gateway support (Istio Gateway + VirtualService, Cilium K8s Gateway API with HTTPRoute). Includes bitnami/postgresql sub-chart, HPA, PVC for blob storage, S3 mode, and 5 ready-to-use example values files.
* **Landing page** — static marketing page at `landing/` with Holo dark design, app UI mockup, 14 format showcase, Demo video placeholder, Docker Compose + Helm quick start tabs, releases link. Deploy with `docker compose --profile landing up -d landing` on port 8080.
* **In-app documentation page** — `/docs` route accessible to all authenticated users; "Documentation" button in the sidebar footer above user info. Two-column layout: left nav with all sections + right scrollable content. Includes Getting Started (auth methods, API token usage, base URL), and full reference pages for all 14 repository formats (Maven, npm, PyPI, Docker, Go, NuGet, Raw, Helm, Cargo, Apt, Yum, Conan, Conda, Terraform) — each with repository URL, authentication config, publish examples, and download/install curl commands. All code blocks have copy-to-clipboard. Base URL is detected dynamically from `window.location.origin` so examples show the correct deployment URL automatically.
* **In-app how-to guides** — seven step-by-step guide articles in the Docs page (Guides section): Creating Repositories (Hosted/Proxy/Group wizard walkthrough), Managing Users, Roles & Privileges (RBAC model: Content Selector → Privilege → Role → User), Content Selectors (CEL expression reference with examples), Security Scanning (OSV vulnerability dashboard + bulk scan), Cleanup Policies (criteria, cron schedule, attach to repo, Run Now), and API Tokens (create, copy-once, Basic Auth, Bearer usage, revoke). Each step includes a screenshot placeholder — add a PNG to `frontend/public/docs/screenshots/<name>.png` to replace the dashed placeholder automatically.
* **Format nav brand icons** — all 14 format buttons in the Docs page left nav now use real brand icons via Simple Icons CDN (`cdn.simpleicons.org`) with emoji fallback when the CDN is unreachable.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

* **Go modules docs** — corrected environment variable from `GONOSUMCHECK` (invalid) to `GONOSUMDB` in both the in-app docs and README.

### 🔒 Security

* **Directory listing blocked** — `http.FileServer` previously exposed directory contents at any path that mapped to a directory in `frontend/dist/` (e.g. `/docs/screenshots/`). The static file handler now returns the SPA root for any directory request that does not contain an `index.html`, preventing enumeration of static asset paths.

## v1.7.0

2026-05-08 — Nexspence v1.7.0

### ✨ Features

- **Conda format handler** (Phase 61) — hosted channel with `repodata.json` generation from DB; `.tar.bz2` and `.conda` package upload/download/delete; proxy mode with upstream URL rewriting so `conda install` works transparently; default upstream `conda-forge`
- **Terraform Registry Mirror** (Phase 62) — service discovery (`/.well-known/terraform.json`); provider versions list, binary upload/download; module versions, upload, `X-Terraform-Get` redirect; proxy mode caches provider binaries from `registry.terraform.io`; works with `terraform init` against a private mirror
- **LDAP external role mapping** (Phase 60) — on every LDAP login, user roles are synced from all group memberships: `admin_group` → `nx-admin`, explicit `role_mappings` entries, and group-name-equals-role-name fallback; same REPLACE semantics as OIDC

## v1.6.0

2026-05-07 — Nexspence v1.6.0

### ✨ Features                                                                                                                                 
* **Phase 58 — Interactive Security Access Map**: New "Access Map" tab in SecurityPage (admin-only). Renders the full RBAC graph — Users → Roles → Privileges → Content Selectors — as a plain SVG with hierarchical columns. Type pills searchable combobox let you pick a starting node; the graph then shows only that node's chain (upstream and downstream). By default, the chains for `admin` and `anonymous` are pre-rendered so the tab is useful on first open. Selecting any node in the SVG updates the selection. A sidebar shows type-specific detai ls (user status/source/roles, role privilege count, privilege CS link, CS expression). Backend: new `GET /api/v1/security/access-graph` handler (admin-only) returns all four entity collections in one response; graph joins are resolved client-side.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
* **Access Map renders only chain nodes**: SVG now renders only nodes that belong to the selected chain instead of all nodes at dim opacity. SVG element count is proportional to the chain size, keeping the graph fast and readable even on large deployments.                
* **Create local user fails with "invalid input: username is required"**: The create-user form was sending `{ username: "…" }` but `domain.User.Username` deserializes from `json:"userId"` (Nexus API compat). Fixed by aligning the form state key to `userId`.

## v1.5.0

2026-05-07 — Nexspence v1.5.0

### ✨ Features

* **Phase 57 — Role Privilege Detail View**: Role cards in SecurityPage → Roles tab now show a clickable privilege-count badge (e.g. "3 privileges ▼"). Expanding a card reveals an inline panel per privilege: type badge, name, linked Content Selector name, and action chips (read/browse/write/delete). Privilege details are fetched lazily on first expand and cached client-side; cache is invalidated when the role is saved.
* **Phase 52 — SAML 2.0 SSO**: SP-initiated SSO via `github.com/crewjam/saml`; supports ADFS, Azure AD (legacy SAML), Okta SAML. Config: `saml.enabled`, `idp_metadata_url`, `sp_entity_id`, `acs_url`. Provisioning: jit / allowlist / manual. Role mapping via `admin_group` + `role_mappings` (REPLACE semantics). Ephemeral RSA-2048 keypair if no PEM configured; HMAC-SHA256 signed RelayState. Fragment-based JWT delivery (`/saml/callback#token=…`). "Sign in with SAML" button on login page. AdminPage → SAML SSO tab with SP config details, metadata download link, and Redis status card.
* Add `deploy/` directory with `nginx-ha.conf` to release package (required for HA mode)
* Add High Availability startup instructions to Quick Start guide

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

* **Roles API returned empty privileges list**: `GET /service/rest/v1/security/roles` always returned `privileges: []` — the DB query did not join `role_privileges`. Fixed with `LEFT JOIN … array_agg` so the roles list now includes privilege IDs; the expand button in the UI now appears correctly.
* **OIDC panic on startup when Keycloak is not yet ready**: `NewRouter` panicked with a stack trace if the IdP was unreachable at boot time. Replaced with a 60-second retry loop (every 3 s) that logs `WARN oidc discovery not ready, retrying in 3s` and only calls `os.Exit(1)` with a clean message after the timeout — handles Keycloak's ~30 s cold-start in Docker Compose.
* **HA Compose `depends_on` invalid project error**: Removed erroneous `depends_on: keycloak` — Docker Compose rejects dependencies on profile-gated services when the profile is not active. The retry loop above handles the race instead.
* Fix tags of images

## v1.3.0

2026-05-06 — Nexspence v1.3.0

### ✨ Features

- **Content Replication (Phase 55):** Push artifacts from a local Nexspence repository to a remote Nexspence instance on a cron schedule. Duplicate detection by asset path, AES-256-GCM-encrypted credentials, skip-and-continue error handling. New `replication_rules` and `replication_history` tables (migration 017). `ReplicationService` with cron scheduler, `TestConnection`, `ListHistory`. Six API endpoints: list/create/update/delete rules, manual run, test connection, list history. Frontend `ReplicationTab` in System Admin with rule cards, inline history table, and create/edit modal.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Monitoring page blank screen:** Backend never included `artifacts_deleted` in `GET /api/v1/metrics`; frontend called `.toLocaleString()` on `undefined`, throwing `TypeError` and crashing the React tree. Fixed by adding `ArtifactsDeleted` atomic counter to the metrics package (incremented on every `DeleteArtifact` call) and guarding the frontend render with `?? 0`.
- **Replication tab blank screen:** Go nil slices serialise to JSON `null`; `ListRules`/`ListHistory` returned `null` instead of `[]`, causing `rules.map()` to throw `TypeError`. Fixed with `make([]T, 0)` on the backend and a `?? []` guard in the frontend query function.

Web UI: `http://localhost:8081`

## Webhook handler tests (Phase 14B.1)

New `internal/api/handlers/webhooks_test.go` with 5 httptest-based cases:

- `GET /webhooks/:id` — 200 with full body, 404 on unknown ID
- `POST /webhooks/:id/test` — 200 with `TestResult` (status + latency_ms) against a live local receiver, 404 on unknown ID, 502 when delivery fails (connection refused)

## Webhook events: repo.updated and repo.deleted (Phase 14B.2+14B.3)

`RepositoryService` now dispatches webhook events on repository lifecycle changes:

- `repo.updated` fired after a successful `Update()` call
- `repo.deleted` fired after a successful `Delete()` call
- New domain constants: `EventRepoUpdated`, `EventRepoDeleted`
- Consistent with existing `repo.created` — fire-and-forget async dispatch, only when a `WebhookDispatcher` is wired

## Search — Last Downloaded timestamp

SearchPage now shows when an artifact was last downloaded:

- Main component row: small `↓ <date>` line under "Modified" date (only when the artifact has been downloaded at least once)
- Expanded asset rows: `↓ <date>` appended inline after `lastModified`
- Falls back to component-level `lastDownloaded` when asset-level is absent
- No backend changes — API already returned the field; frontend types updated to expose it

## Routing Rules (Phase 14C)

Group repositories now enforce routing rules during artifact resolution:

- Full CRUD API: `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /service/rest/v1/routing-rules`
- `mode=BLOCK`: members whose paths match any regex matcher are skipped
- `mode=ALLOW`: only members whose paths match at least one matcher are tried
- Fail-open: missing or unconfigured rule allows all paths through
- AdminPage → Routing Rules tab: create/edit/delete rules with dynamic matcher list
- RepositoriesPage: group repo create/edit modals expose a Routing Rule selector

## Bug Fixes

### Vulnerability scan fails after container restart (`MANIFEST_UNKNOWN`)

Docker image manifests were stored at a path derived from the DB blob store config
(`./data/blobs/default`), which resolves to `/app/data/blobs/default` inside the
container — outside the persistent volume mounted at `/data/blobs`. After a restart
the directory was empty, so Trivy received `MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` from the registry.

**Fix:** `syncBlobStorePaths()` runs at startup and updates every local blob store's
`path` in the DB to `filepath.Join(basePath, storeName)`, matching the configured
`NEXSPENCE_STORAGE_LOCAL_BASE_PATH`. Hosted repos now survive restarts without
requiring a re-push.

### Proxy Docker repos always fail scan with "image not found"

Two separate issues caused scans to fail on proxy-type Docker repositories even when
the image was visibly cached:

1. `repoproxy.ServeGET` wrote cached blobs to `d.BlobStore` (base path `/data/blobs`)
   but `RegisterStoredBlob` recorded the "default" blob store ID (path
   `/data/blobs/default`). On read, `PhysicalStore` looked in the wrong directory.
   Fixed by using `base.ResolveBlobStore` so the write location and the DB record
   always point to the same physical store.

2. When the cached blob file was missing (e.g. after a path change), `ServeGET`
   returned 502 instead of falling through to an upstream fetch. Fixed: a blob-get
   error is now treated as a cache miss — the asset is refetched from upstream and
   re-cached at the correct location.
